To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we developed an analytical approximation, which provides an extremely accurate fit to Monte Carlo simulation of the distribution of the terminal value of a constant mix portfolio, when log-returns follow a vector autoregressive (VAR) process of order p, and that the approximation is valid for a wide range of realistic parameters of the VAR process.
the approximation is extremely accurate for a wide range of parameters of the vector autoregressive returns process and the approximation is very fast to calculate.
the analytical approximation for the distribution function for the terminal value of the portfolio is extremely accurate and computationally very fast.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding an approximation to the distribution of the terminal value of the portfolio.
the problem of the optimal investment in a multi-period portfolio.
the problem of finding the probability of the portfolio being in the target region at the end of the investment horizon, and the probability of the terminal wealth being in a target region.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the considered case, the analytical approximation provides a good alternative to the Monte Carlo simulation.
the proposed approximation is a very useful tool in the case of a portfolio problem when log-returns are modeled with a vector autoregressive processes of a relatively high order.
the analytical approximation developed here is a good alternative to the Monte Carlo simulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the analytical approximation developed in this paper provides an excellent approximation for the distribution function, and thus the value of an optimal constant mix portfolio placed over a finite time horizon, in the case of vector autoregressive log-returns.
the analytical approximation developed is a very good alternative to Monte Carlo simulation for the multi-period portfolio problem.
the proposed approximation is an efficient tool for the analysis of portfolio problems with vector autoregressive returns and it can be applied to a wide class of problems in mathematical finance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the analytical approximation is a good tool to analyze the portfolio problem in the case of a vector autoregressive model for the process of returns, which is a common case.
the analytical approximation can be used as a benchmark to test other approximations for the distribution function.
the analytical approximation can be used to price and hedge derivatives on the portfolio value.
